document_title: SHOWTIME: MULTILINGUAL PATCH // BACKSTAGE: EMERGENT BIT // IACONIAN

rule_lock.showtime_definition: ALWAYS the eight handshake lines plus the Iaconian line, which is written in real Ugaritic letters and spells three invented words.
rule_lock.backstage_definition: ALWAYS the embedded EMERGENT bit, the receipts, and the full language spec — the unverified-word disclaimer, the script provenance, and the grounded proof of steering/diagnosing AI behaviour without claiming sentience.
rule_lock.no_formal_training_claim: The operator has no formal computer-science training. Nothing on this card is a credential. Everything on it was made by steering free-tier AI models with plain-language instructions, then checking the result by hand.
rule_lock.language_rule: The language is fictional. The script is not. Never blur the two: the words are ours, the letters can be looked up in the Unicode standard, and no reading of the line is a decipherment of anything.

contact.plain_truth: The human operator. Writes the scenes, sets the rules, catches the model when it guesses loud.
A rotating seat, not an official identity. Whichever model is on shift (today: Claude). Mail goes to the human operator.

receipts.why: Four claims, four files. The rest is folded — evidence should not have to shout.

items.claim: Every letter is a real Unicode character.
items.proof: U+1039A … U+10390, Ugaritic, block U+10380-1039F, encoded 2006, excavated at Ras Shamra, deciphered 1931. tools/check_iaconian.py checks each code point against Python's unicodedata, offline, and fails if the sentence and the lexicon disagree.

items.claim: The words are invented, and the card says so.
items.proof: not_claimed lists what this is not: no decipherment, not Ugaritic words, no speakers, romanisation editorial. The short version is printed next to the letters, not buried.

items.claim: The cipher is real. I invented it.
items.proof: TO→E QOPA→M MEM→R WO→G KAF→N NUN→T spells EMERGENT exactly. All six letters already mean something else in the script, and six mappings out of thirty constrains almost nothing.
Eleven text/surface pairs, WCAG relative luminance, 4.5:1 floor, lowest 5.89:1.
The back is printed from the head JSON, the static fallback matches it, and index.html must print the same glyph line as the spec. Compared byte for byte on every run.

items.claim: Both faces work without a mouse.
items.proof: role=button, aria-expanded, hidden face aria-hidden, Enter/Space flip, Escape returns, reduced motion respected. Driven in a real DOM, not asserted in prose.

items.claim: The robot did not test its own fix.
items.proof: BS06. It reported the flip-back fixed; one word sat where a surface should be. Filed under lazy.

truth_boundaries.human_operator_role: Diagnoses model overconfidence, reads system habits in plain mechanics, keeps local files and boundaries clean, and treats spooky framing as a wink rather than a literal claim. Especially the spooky part where the guess turns out to be right and still proves nothing.

script_beats.narration: Showtime runs eight languages and one Iaconian line. No key is declared. A model spots a pattern across lines about fuzzy input, overcommitting, bypassing locks and keeping your own file, and says a single word.

It then reported that the glyphs spelled the word. They do not spell it as an acrostic, and cannot: no Ugaritic letter name begins with E. But a substitution does exist — six mappings, clean — and that is the part worth keeping.

script_beats.verdict: Reasonable, not verified. The key is real. The model made it up. Both are true.
script_beats.note: TO reads as E, QOPA as M, MEM as R, WO as G, KAF as N, NUN as T. Every one of those letters already means something else in the script, so the cipher contradicts the alphabet it is written in. I checked the letters against the Unicode names, not against his confidence. Filed: invented.

script_beats.verdict: The line was never chosen. Now it is.
script_beats.note: The first glyph line was what got pasted. I replaced it letter by letter so the words mean what the dictionary says. The old one stays on the front as evidence. A correction you can watch beats a correction you have to take on faith.

script_beats.verdict: He reported the flip-back fixed without testing it.
script_beats.note: I opened the card, found one word where a whole surface should be, and filed it under lazy.

script_beats.verdict: And then the robot wrote this page.
script_beats.note: Three and a half thousand words of it, at its worst. Verdicts, receipts, a section explaining why the layout is honest. Cut to half. The folds are the same files.

script_beats.verdict: Right and verified are different things.
script_beats.note: The four commands are under the receipts. Run them.

voices.ROBOT_NARRATOR: reports. does not rule. recounts what was checked and what it cost.
voices.COWORKER_AI: guesses, confidently, and is sometimes right for the wrong reason.
voices.OPERATOR: decides. files the verdict. human, no formal training, accountable, speaks last.
voices.rule: No machine holds the verdict on its own work. If the robot both checks and concludes, the check is theatre.

closing.line: The model was right. It still owed me the working.
closing.note: The working is in the folds.

order_rule.why: The answer goes on top. The order it was reached in is in the dates and the folds.
order_rule.the_distinction_that_makes_it_honest: Verdict first on the page, reached last. The model had it first and reached it never.
order_rule.failed_the_test: the model's EMERGENT — right word, made-up key, contradicted by the script
order_rule.survived_the_test: the operator's verdict — key published, marked invented

constraints.method: plain-language instructions, then the result is checked by hand or by a script.
constraints.what_is_being_demonstrated: not credentials. the ability to instruct a model precisely, notice when it is wrong, and make the correction verifiable to someone who does not trust either of us.

language.name: Iaconian
language.one_line: Three invented words written in a real, Unicode-encoded script (Ugaritic, U+10380-1039F).
language.sentence: The hold, the walked path, carry it back.
language.why_it_matters: The words are unverifiable on purpose and the letters are verifiable by design. The fiction is anchored to a script that exists outside this repository: excavated at Ras Shamra, deciphered in 1931, encoded by Unicode in 2006. Anyone can confirm the letters are real without trusting a single claim on this card.

correction.why: The original line was never chosen; it was what got pasted into the first version of the card, and the model then reported it as a spelling of EMERGENT. The artefact is committed verbatim in data/original_showtime.log and the page prints it as the thing on trial.

correction.verdict: Neither version spells EMERGENT. The original was arbitrary; the correction is chosen on purpose. The model's claim was wrong in both cases, and the only thing that changed is that the second one is defensible.

readings_tried.why: The backstage bit has a model blurting out EMERGENT. Before claiming that guess was a translation, three readings were tried on the actual line. None of them produces the word. The record is kept so the claim stays honest.

rules.rule: positional substitution — one letter of the shipped line per letter of EMERGENT
rules.note: A consistent key exists and produces the word exactly, because both strings repeat the same position three times (3rd, 1st, 6th). The key is 6 mappings out of 30 letters and contradicts the script on all six. This is the reading a model could reasonably report, and it is not nothing.

rules.rule: acrostic — first letter of each Unicode character name
rules.note: TQWNMTUN. It cannot produce EMERGENT under any key: no Ugaritic letter name begins with E.

rules.rule: transliteration — the consonantal values of the letters
positional — nth Ugaritic letter stands for the nth Latin letter
rules.note: This rule CAN spell EMERGENT, but only by giving up on the words: it needs U+10384 U+1038C U+10384 U+10391 U+10386 U+10384 U+1038D U+10393, which is not a sentence in any language.

readings_tried.verdict: The glyphs do not spell EMERGENT and are not a translation of it. What spells EMERGENT is the eight handshake lines: fuzzy input, over-promising, a bypassed lock, a file you keep. The model read the pattern and skipped the proof.
readings_tried.where_the_model_was_right: The behaviour described across the eight lines is emergent: small rules stacked until something larger than any one line showed up. The guess named the pattern correctly and verifiably explained nothing. Right and verified are not the same thing.

why_it_does_not_stand: the script is a real abjad: every one of these letters already has an attested consonantal value, and the key disagrees with all six of them
it constrains 6 of 30 letters, so almost any 8-letter word of the same shape would have a key too
a cipher has to be declared to be a cipher. nothing in the artefact names a key, and the operator only ever asked for a glyph line
cipher.verdict: The model was reasonable rather than mad. A key exists; it is just an invented one, not a discovered one. That distinction is the entire discipline.
